title: Network lab 5: Routing between VLANs (Packet Tracer)
summary: Carry both VLANs to a router over one trunk, give each VLAN a gateway on a subinterface, and route between them.

script.intro: VLANs keep people apart. Sometimes they need to meet, through a router we control. Today: one trunk, two subinterfaces, two gateways.
script.outro: Routing joins the VLANs again, which is exactly why the next labs add switch hardening and access lists.
steps: Open your lab 4 file and save a copy. Add a 1941 (or 2911) router and cable switch Gi0/1 to router G0/0. On the switch CLI: Type the commands on screen, then check the result with the show command.
On the router CLI: Type the commands on screen, then check the result with the show command.
From guest-1, ping staff-1 (192.168.10.11). It works now, because the router joins the VLANs. Good for printing; bad for security: guests can reach staff computers again.
VLANs, a trunk and a router. Before the access list, lab 6 hardens the switch itself.
